subject: Post-call: hosting constraints, migration options & proposed exit plan
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Sofia Morales <s.morales@nimbushealth.com>, Rajesh Iyer <rajesh.iyer@nimbushealth.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 11 Mar 2027 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Quick recap + next step options (hosting + migration)

Hi Sofia / Rajesh —

Thanks again for the productive discovery earlier today. I wanted to capture the areas we agreed to validate and propose a pragmatic next step so we can keep momentum on the proof-of-concept. High level notes: 

- Primary goals: deploy clinical triage assistant to production for 1 US region, target 99th-p50 latency under 300ms for short prompts (~100 tokens), initial throughput ~15 req/s burst to 50 for morning peaks.
- Data/security constraints: PHI in prompts, customer-controlled keys preferred, inbound VPC peering is acceptable but traffic must stay in their VPC for PHI retention policy.
- Migration context: current stack uses a managed LLM API (vendor: PromptWorks) for experiments, and there is an on-prem GPU staging cluster (older GTX/Tesla hardware) used for internal testing. They will need a path off PromptWorks eventually.

Hosting options we discussed (summary):
1) Hosted API (Redwood): fastest onboarding, we handle key management, strong cost controls; good fit if they can accept non-customer-managed network for requests (encrypted in transit, customer data policy ok with vendor process).
2) Dedicated capacity: reserved GPU pool in our infra with customer-only tenancy. Predictable throughput and ability to pin model/quantization profile. Sits behind Redwood-managed networking but can be logically isolated.
3) Private VPC / On-prem bundle: full customer VPC peering or on-prem appliance, customer controls keys and network. Necessary if security policy requires zero-third-party processing of PHI.

Based on the constraints listed, it sounds like Private VPC is the safer long-term target, while Dedicated gives the most straightforward short-term ramp if they need isolation without full on-prem. Hosted API could be an acceptable interim for non-PHI workloads.

Next steps (proposed):
- Deliver a short mutual-action-plan (MAP) with timelines for POC, compliance gating, and cutover options (attached: Nimbus-MAP-v1.xlsx).
- Aditya: can you capture rough perf profile (model candidates, quantization impact) and thumb rule cost for Dedicated vs Private?
- Rajesh / Sofia: confirm whether initial POC will include PHI or if we can restrict to de-identified data for the first 60 days. If PHI is required from day one, we need to move to Private VPC conversation immediately.

I'll loop in Marissa from CS for onboarding checklist once we have the preferred path.

Thanks —

Jordan Blake
Senior AE, Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwood.com
+1 415 555 0192

Attachments: Nimbus-MAP-v1.xlsx
From: Rajesh Iyer <rajesh.iyer@nimbushealth.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Sofia Morales <s.morales@nimbushealth.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 11 Mar 2027 18:46:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Quick recap + next step options (hosting + migration)

Jordan —

Thanks for the summary, that captures it well. A couple clarifications from our side: 

- PHI: our legal says any unencrypted processing outside our VPC is a no-go for the production rollout. For the POC we can use de-identified data for model tuning.
- Legacy GPU cluster: that environment is a hard constraint for now — it's only for lab experiments and lacks autoscaling. We will not consider it production.
- Vendor migration: we are interested in a plan to extract prompts/usage patterns from PromptWorks for parity testing. We may also want a short period of dual-write for validation.

Can you provide the Dedicated vs Private rough cost range and what effort is needed from our infra team for VPC peering? Also, add me as primary contact for compliance artifacts.

Regards,
Rajesh
Director, Platform Engineering
Nimbus Health

Date: Fri, 12 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Quick recap + next step options (hosting + migration)

Rajesh / team —

Great call. I sketched a short tech note attached (hosting-matrix-quote.pdf) that outlines latency expectations and infra work per hosting mode. A few quick bullets: 

- Hosted API: ~2–3 days to get a POC environment, no infra work from Nimbus, but PHI restriction prevents production use. Good for model tuning with de-identified samples. Estimated cloud usage: $X–$Y per 100k tokens (we'll calibrate after model selection).
- Dedicated capacity: we can provision a reserved pool (8–16 A100-equivalent GPUs) — estimated procurement lead 2–4 weeks. Requires routing CIDR allowlist and minimal firewall changes. Supports customer keying via KMS integration. Estimated monthly committed spend range: $COMMITTED_RANGE.
- Private VPC / On-prem: tight control — requires 3–4 weeks of infra coordination for VPC peering + routing, or 6–8 weeks for on-prem appliance install and validation. We will need a point of contact with access to their network team for VPN / BGP config.

Migration notes:
- From PromptWorks: we can set up a dual-write (requests logged to both) for a validation window. We recommend exporting 30 days of traffic for prompt distribution analysis.
- From legacy GPU cluster: we recommend against direct lift-and-shift; instead, benchmark representative workloads on Dedicated and do a staged cutover.

I'll attach the hosting matrix and rough numbers. Jordan — happy to jump on a technical sync with Rajesh next week.

Best,
Aditya Rao
Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
aditya.rao@redwood.com

From: Sofia Morales <s.morales@nimbushealth.com>

Date: Sat, 13 Mar 2027 11:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Quick recap + next step options (hosting + migration)

Jordan / Aditya —

Appreciate the clear options. Internal next steps from Nimbus: 

1) We will run a de-identification pass and confirm scope for the POC (target: de-identified for first 45 days).
2) Rajesh will share a roster for our infra folks for VPC peering coordination; expect an introduction early next week.
3) Please send a short one-page statement listing data flow for Private VPC and Dedicated modes for our security review (include KMS flow and where logs are stored).

If the one-pager looks good, we can sign the MAP and target a Dedicated POC first (to get predictable SLAs), with Private VPC as the production cutover plan.

Thanks —
Sofia Morales
Product Owner, Clinical AI
Nimbus Health
